themes.naming: A name misdescribes what a value holds or a function does, is vague, lacks a verb, or omits a type suffix (*_id, is_*).
themes.vocabulary: Coined jargon, a synonym for an existing concept, or an overloaded or banned word where the project already has a word.
themes.code_placement: Code sits in the wrong module or layer, or a layer knows app or domain concepts it should not.
themes.reinvents_existing: New code re-implements or duplicates an existing primitive, model, helper or tool.
themes.one_source_of_truth: One fact, list, rule or approach is kept in two places that must agree.
themes.needless_abstraction: A new type, wrapper, function, flag, check or special case the goal does not need; a simpler design exists.
themes.dead_code: Code, fields or branches that nothing reads or can reach.
themes.scope_creep: The diff carries unrequested features or unrelated edits, or is far bigger than the ask.
themes.backcompat: A compatibility shim, legacy path or half-finished migration kept instead of a clean migration.
themes.dict_any: dict[str, Any], Any or an untyped dict where a model with named fields belongs.
themes.weak_types: Imprecise types: str for a closed set, Optional on a required field, a missing annotation or exhaustive match.
themes.fallback_or_fabrication: A silent default, fallback, placeholder or made-up value stands in for data or hides a failure.
themes.boundary_validation: Validation, None-handling or raising is misplaced or missing: Optional deferral, missing guard, soft return, broad except.
themes.data_model: What a record stores and how: identity, derivable or duplicate fields, one shape versus several, persistence layout.
themes.verbose_prose: Prose (prompt, tool description, doc, comment) longer than its content needs.
themes.prompt_design: What LLM-facing text says: role, purpose, procedure, what the model already knows.
themes.llm_contract: Work given to the LLM, or a rule left in prompt prose, that code or schema should derive or enforce.
themes.prose_accuracy: Prose states something untrue, overclaims, frames the point wrong, or does not parse.
themes.comments_and_docs: A comment, docstring or doc restates code, narrates the edit, points elsewhere, sits at the wrong altitude or should not exist.
themes.product_copy: Wording of user-facing or model-facing product copy, as distinct from its length.
themes.ux_behavior: What the UI shows or how it behaves; visual encoding choices.
themes.design_direction: The reviewer rejects, redirects or specifies the design or product behaviour; judging it needs product context.
themes.correctness_bug: A logic error, missed edge case, unmet real-world requirement, or a workaround instead of the root cause.
themes.tests: A test is missing, weak, skipped, trivial, circular or restates the code.
themes.gates: The reviewer asks for a rule to be enforced mechanically or written down, or objects to a gate's design, weakening or evasion.
themes.ignored_feedback: The agent did not do what was asked or agreed, deferred it, or reintroduced something rejected.
themes.readability: Code a reader cannot follow locally: roundabout control flow, unexplained sentinels, long functions.
themes.hardcoded_values: Hardcoded paths, constants, magic values or facts that should be derived or declared once.
themes.interface_shape: A function or tool takes the wrong inputs: paths instead of ids, whole objects, generic passthroughs.
themes.review_guide: The PR text or review guide is miscalibrated: wrong or missing decision flags, unflagged concepts.
themes.question_only: A clarifying question with no correction implied.
themes.praise_or_signoff: Explicit praise, approval, acceptance or sign-off.
themes.other: Feature ideas, follow-up requests, housekeeping, performance, security and one-offs.
